name: Secure Signal Admin API
description: Next.js Route Handlers backing the Secure Signal admin/authority dashboard and mobile app. Staff/rider routes rely on Supabase SSR cookies. Device-facing routes (mobile app → backend) use a separate shared-secret header instead, since there's no user session on the device.

session.notes: Sign in via the web app or POST to /auth (Supabase hosted). The browser automatically attaches the sb-access-token cookie. Server-only routes verify it via createServerClient() and read role from public.profiles.

device.notes: Required on every device-facing endpoint (incident report/log, device register, ping ack, and the legacy incident/track equivalents). The value is the DEVICE_API_KEY env var configured on the server — request it from whoever manages the deployment; it is not something the client derives or generates. Missing/wrong key → 401. Server has no key configured → 503 (fails closed).

rateLimits.notes: Fixed-window, per the key shown. Exceeding it returns 429 { error: "too many requests" }. All limits fail open on infra error — a rate-limiter outage never blocks a legitimate request.

commonErrors.400: Validation failed — body did not match the Zod schema. Body includes an `issues` array with details on most routes.
commonErrors.401: Unauthenticated/unauthorized — no Supabase session, or missing/wrong X-Device-Key.
commonErrors.403: Forbidden — signed in but role not allowed for this resource.
commonErrors.429: Rate limited — see rateLimits above. Back off and retry after the window.
commonErrors.500: Server or upstream (Supabase/Stripe/FCM) error. Body shape: { error: string }.
commonErrors.503: Endpoint not configured — a required server env var is missing (DEVICE_API_KEY, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, MAILCHIMP_API_KEY/MAILCHIMP_AUDIENCE_ID depending on route).

endpoints.description: OAuth callback URL used by Supabase after email-link / OAuth sign in. Exchanges the `code` query param for a session cookie and redirects to `next` or `/`.

query.code: string (required) — Supabase auth code from the redirect URL
query.next: string (optional) — path to redirect to after exchange, default `/`

responses.302: Redirect to origin + next (or /login?error=oauth on failure)

endpoints.description: List the signed-in user's emergency contacts.
Add an emergency contact for the signed-in user.
Update one of the signed-in user's emergency contacts.
Remove an emergency contact.
List emergency contacts, optionally filtered to one rider.
Add an emergency contact on behalf of any rider.
Update any rider's emergency contact.
Remove any rider's emergency contact.

Register (or confirm) that a device_uuid belongs to a user_id. Idempotent — a matching (device_uuid, user_id) pair already on file is a no-op, not a duplicate. If device_uuid exists under a *different* user_id, ownership is deliberately NOT reassigned (returned with a `note` field instead) — that's not something an unauthenticated device call should be able to trigger silently.

body.device_uuid: string (required) — the hardware's own id, not a uuid
body.user_id: string (required) — the driver's profiles.id; degrades to null if it doesn't resolve to a real profile, never fails the request

200.note: string (present only when device_uuid belongs to a different user)

endpoints.description: Current incident-creation endpoint. Sent once when an SOS/fall trigger first fires.

body.user_id: string (optional) — driver id; degrades to null if unresolvable
body.device_id: string (optional) — the hardware's own id, stored as-is
body.incident_type: string (optional) — 'SOS Button' | 'SOS Volume keys' | 'SOS USB' | 'SOS Fall Detected'; anything else is stored as null rather than rejected

endpoints.description: Location breadcrumb for an active incident. Sent roughly every 10 seconds while the incident is in progress.
List incidents for the dashboard. Filterable by date/status/type/search/location radius, sortable.

query.lat, lng, radius: number — filter to incidents within radius meters of (lat,lng) (optional, all three required together)

endpoints.description: Legacy incident-creation endpoint — predates /api/incidents/report. Kept alive (and hardened the same way) for older mobile app builds; new integrations should use /api/incidents/report instead.

body.device_uuid: string (optional) — the hardware's own id, stored as-is into device_id

endpoints.description: List incidents. Optional date filter (YYYY-MM-DD, UTC). Returns up to 500 rows newest first.

query.date: string (optional) — YYYY-MM-DD UTC; filters occurred_at to that day

endpoints.description: Fetch a single incident.
Transition an incident's status. Marks the row read. Writes a `logs` entry.
Sends a stop-emergency FCM push to the incident's device (notification body: `STOP_EMERGENCY-{device_uuid}`, matched exactly by the mobile app). Writes a `logs` entry.

409.error: incident has no device | device has no registered push token

endpoints.description: Legacy breadcrumb endpoint — predates /api/incidents/log. Kept alive (and hardened the same way) for older mobile app builds; new integrations should use /api/incidents/log instead.
Read the most recent 100 breadcrumb points for an incident, newest first.
Send a ping to a device. Inserts a `pings` row (status=sent) and best-effort FCM push using the device's registered token.
Device callback — marks a ping as `received`. Called by the device after processing the FCM push.
Sends an FCM push telling a device to start its standard (non-emergency) location pings. Notification body: `START-{device_uuid}`, matched exactly by the mobile app.
Sends an FCM push telling a device to stop its standard location pings. Notification body: `STOP-{device_uuid}`, matched exactly by the mobile app.

Device reports its current location for a specific ping, updating pings.lat/lng/accuracy for the row matching ping_id. The admin ping map re-centers on this location and draws accuracy as a radius circle around the marker.
Public contact form submission. Stores a row in `contacts` for the admin to review.
List the latest 100 contact submissions.
Public footer newsletter signup. Upserts the subscriber into Mailchimp via PUT with status_if_new — never re-subscribes someone who previously unsubscribed.
Backs the public support-chat widget. Proxies to the Anthropic Messages API with a fixed system prompt.

body.messages: Array<{ role: 'user'|'assistant', content: string (1-4000 chars) }> (1-20 items, required)

503.error: Chat is not configured yet. Set ANTHROPIC_API_KEY to enable it.

endpoints.description: Server-side proxy for Nominatim address search (adds a proper User-Agent per its usage policy, which a client-side fetch can't reliably set). Used by the seller onboarding area-picker.

200.results: Array<{ label: string, lat: number, lng: number }>

endpoints.description: Promotes the caller to the 'seller' role once their seller_profiles row has all required fields (business_name, services, area_lat/lng/radius). Uses the service-role client deliberately — profiles.role is not something a session client should ever be trusted to set directly.

400.error: Finish both onboarding steps before submitting.

403.error: This role can't start seller onboarding.

endpoints.description: Creates a 'contact us' service request routed to Secure Signal staff, not the seller. Body: { seller_user_id: uuid, service_type: towing|battery|tire|lockout, message: string (1-2000 chars) }. Enforcement of 'seller never sees this' lives at the seller_inquiries RLS layer — the seller role has no read policy on that table at all, not just a UI omission.

403.error: only riders can request a service

endpoints.description: Updates a seller_inquiries row's status (new/contacted/closed) as staff work the queue. Body: { status: new|contacted|closed }.

Upserts the caller's review for the given seller — one review per rider per seller, re-submitting edits it. Requires the rider to already have a seller_inquiries row for that seller (checked here for a clear error message, and separately enforced by seller_reviews' own INSERT policy). Body: { rating: 1-5, body?: string (max 2000 chars) }.

403.error: only riders can leave a review | Contact us about this seller before leaving a review.

endpoints.description: Sets or clears hidden_by_admin on a review (moderation — hidden reviews stop showing to riders/sellers but stay visible to staff and to the reviewing rider). Body: { hidden: boolean }.

Self-service, irreversible account deletion. Hard-deletes the auth user, which cascades to profile/emergency_contacts/subscriptions/seller_profiles/sent incident_messages and the profile_images storage folder. devices/incidents/logs are anonymized (user_id set null) rather than deleted, per the existing on-delete-set-null schema design — those are safety/audit records, not personal data.
endpoints.auth: session (acts only on the caller's own id — no target-user param)

endpoints.description: Stripe webhook endpoint. Verifies signature with STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET, upserts `subscriptions` rows, writes a logs entry.

subscriptionMetadata.supabase_user_id: Required key in subscription.metadata so the webhook can attach the row to a profile.

Incident.location: geography(Point, 4326) — kept in sync from lat/lng by a trigger; prefer lat/lng in API bodies
Incident.device_id: string | null — the hardware's own device_uuid, stored directly (a text column; NOT a uuid FK to devices.id, despite the column name)

IncidentLog.device_id: string | null — same convention as Incident.device_id

seller: seller_profile: CRUD self (business details, service area)
admin: subscription: read all, write via Stripe webhook

notes: RLS is the source of truth for row-level access on session-based routes. Route handlers also enforce role checks server-side.

Device-facing routes (incident report/log, device register, ping ack) intentionally bypass RLS via the service-role client: RLS's SELECT policies only allow a row's own owner or staff to read it back, which an anonymous device request is neither — even reading back its own just-inserted row would otherwise fail.

incidents.device_id / incident_logs.device_id are text columns holding the hardware's own device_uuid directly — not a uuid FK to devices.id, despite the column name and what older code comments in this repo may say.
Stripe webhook requires the raw request body — Next.js route handlers receive it via req.text().
FCM uses firebase-admin (server-only). The web client config is NOT compatible with admin — use a service account JSON to populate FIREBASE_PRIVATE_KEY.
FCM push notification bodies are a client-parsed contract, not just display text: stop standard pings = 'STOP-{uuid}', start standard pings = 'START-{uuid}', stop emergency = 'STOP_EMERGENCY-{uuid}'.
Use `application/json` content-type on all write requests.
